key_insight: Overparameterized two-qubit quantum neural networks can “grok”: they first overfit, then later generalize, often after an epoch-wise double-descent spike in test error.
engineering_relevance: Training dynamics in variational quantum circuits are highly sensitive to depth, learning rate, and regularization, so adding light weight-norm control can stabilize generalization in practical QML workflows.
method: Complete SU(4) parameterization on a 2-qubit QNN
Sweep circuit depth, learning rate, and weight decay to track training/test dynamics
Add weak explicit weight-norm regularization to prevent late-stage generalization decay
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical results showing grokking and epoch-wise double descent in test error, with late-stage recovery to generalization under certain hyperparameter settings.
watch_item: The stabilization effect is demonstrated on a small two-qubit system, so transfer to larger noisy hardware circuits may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Grokking and epoch-wise double descent in quantum neural networks
